## Summary (human-written)
<!-- Write this yourself, not with an AI tool. 2-5 sentences: the problem, why
     this approach, and what you checked yourself. -->

1. add proper remat support for HybridEP
2. add moe/README.md as a backend selection guidance

## Why
HybridEP dispatch and combine run outside torch_remat regions. Consequently,
DefaultActivationRematConfig replays both during backward even though its documented
policy retains EP communication. Users also lack a single guide comparing the
supported EP execution paths and their graph, precision, and memory constraints.

**Example.** One forward/backward through a routed-expert layer normally needs
one dispatch and one combine in the forward, plus one call to each primitive
for gradient computation. Activation remat can add another replay of the
forward communication pair:

| Policy | Extra communication before this PR | Extra communication after this PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| No remat | None | None |
| Default remat | 1 extra dispatch and 1 extra combine | None |
| Full remat | 1 extra dispatch and 1 extra combine | 1 extra dispatch and 1 extra combine |

The default policy now retains the forward communication results for expert
recomputation. Normal forward and gradient communication still run; full remat
continues to replay communication as requested.

## What changed
- Declare HybridEP dispatch/combine regions controlled together by `ep_communication`,
  matching DeepEP. Retain counts and scores consumed outside regions.
- Pass the forward handle through a CPU tensor ID because torch_remat 0.2.2 accepts
  only tensor region outputs. Garbage collection releases cache entries. A CPU
  lookup op keeps autograd setup contexts traceable with FakeTensor/AOT. Upstream
  opaque-output support is tracked in [remat issue #10](https://github.com/meta-pytorch/remat/issues/10).
- Add an EP backend selection guide beside MoE, with configuration examples,
  remat semantics, capacity considerations, and links to public dependency guides.
  No backend is removed or added.
- Mechanically share the existing DeepEP test harness with HybridEP, then check
  communication counts, exact loss/gradients, and graph capture. Run HybridEP tests
  after its existing CI installer.

## Alternatives considered
- Retain the whole MoE call: would also retain expert compute that the default
  policy intends to recompute.
- Return the existing opaque handle from the region: current torch_remat rejects
  it. The tensor-only contract comes from meta-pytorch/remat#2; upstream opaque
  output support would allow removal of the tensor-ID cache.

## User-facing changes
| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| HybridEP communication replays under default remat | Default/custom saved policies retain it; full remat still replays it |
| Backend constraints scattered across recipes and implementation | `torchtitan/models/common/moe/README.md` describes the available choices |

## Numerics
No changes to routing, expert computation, checkpoint parameter names, or precision.
Against main `ff96670a2`, DeepSeek V3 debug-model training with FSDP2 x EP2 on two
GB300 GPUs produced bitwise-identical TensorBoard loss and grad_norm for all 10
steps, with seed 42 and deterministic execution. Validation used
`scripts/loss_compare.py --steps 10 --no-seed-checkpoint --metrics loss,grad_norm`,
exporting main's metrics and asserting equality on the branch with `--import-result`.

## Testing
- `pre-commit run --all-files`: passed.
- Focused MoE, transform, and config-validation CPU tests: 73 passed. The new
  FakeTensor backward test catches host scalar reads in autograd setup contexts.
- HybridEP GPU remat tests: 3 passed on two GB300 GPUs. Blocking and nonblocking
  dispatch both match no-remat loss/input/router/expert gradients exactly, with
  expected communication counts; saved communication also survives CUDA graph replay.
- AOT-compiled FakeTensor dispatch/combine forward and backward: passed.
- HybridEP dependency for local GPU tests: public hybrid-ep commit `4e890fd`.

**What this PR does.** It wraps HybridEP dispatch and combine in `remat.region`s keyed by `ep_communication`, as DeepEP already does. Region outputs must be tensors, so the forward now returns a CPU `handle_id` instead of the opaque `DispatchHandle`; a module cache maps the id back to the handle. A new CPU custom op `hybridep.get_handle` resolves the id inside setup_context. The PR also adds an EP backend selection guide (`models/common/moe/README.md`), extends the DeepEP GPU remat test harness to HybridEP, and runs those tests in CI after the HybridEP installer.

**Example.** `graph_trainer_deepseek_v3_debugmodel_hybridep()` (`disable_accelerator_graphs = False`, nonblocking dispatch):
```
main:  dispatch -> getitem[3] (opaque handle) -> combine / combine_bwd
       every node CUDA-graph compatible -> cuda_graph_pass wraps the step
PR:    dispatch -> getitem[3] (CPU handle_id) -> hybridep.get_handle(handle_id)
       get_handle: only tensor is CPU -> is_cuda_graph_node_compatible == False
       -> "Skipping cuda_graph: graph is not compatible ..." (warning), eager step
```

CI won't catch it because both graph-trainer HybridEP integration tests disable accelerator graphs. Fix: delete `get_handle`, pass `handle_id` to `combine_bwd`/`dispatch_bwd`, save it with `save_for_backward`, and resolve the cache entry in the CUDA impls. This deletes the op and keeps FakeTensor tracing clean.

- `torchtitan/distributed/deepep/hybridep.py:217-221` -- duplicates DeepEP's handle-id cache scheme; share one helper so remat#10 removes it in one place.
- `tests/unit_tests/cpu/models/common/test_moe.py:165` -- tests `distributed/deepep/hybridep.py`; move it under `tests/unit_tests/cpu/distributed/`.
- `tests/unit_tests/gpu/distributed/test_deepep_activation_checkpoint.py:342` -- fold `capture` into `_check_hybridep_activation_checkpointing` instead of repeating the config.
- Scope: the backend selection guide is independent of the remat fix. Consider landing it separately so the remat fix can be reviewed on its own.

- Gate: the problem is real on main. HybridEP's ops ran outside any region, so under `DefaultActivationRematConfig` they were recomputed (code outside regions is always recomputed), which contradicts the policy docstring. Fixing it in the dispatcher is the right layer, and the opaque-output workaround has a TODO pointing at meta-pytorch/remat#10.

**Verdict: Approve -- please address the items below before merging.** The CUDA-graph regression from the last review is fixed: `hybridep.get_handle` is gone, and a new graph_trainer test guards against it coming back.

**What changed since the last review.** The backward ops (`combine_bwd`, `dispatch_bwd`) now take `handle_id: Tensor`, the same way `combine` does. They resolve `_handle_cache[handle_id.item()]` only inside the real CUDA implementations, so setup_context no longer traces a CPU-only op. setup_context keeps `handle_id` as a ctx attribute rather than calling `save_for_backward`. The reason is that saved-tensor hooks could copy the tensor and let the original, which owns the cache entry, be collected. The GPU test exercises this with a cloning `saved_tensors_hooks`.

**Example.** `graph_trainer_deepseek_v3_debugmodel_hybridep()` traced graph:
```
previous rev: dispatch -> handle_id -> hybridep.get_handle(handle_id)   # pure-CPU node -> cuda_graph skipped
HEAD:         dispatch -> handle_id -> combine(x, handle_id) / combine_bwd(g, s, handle_id)
              every node mixes CUDA and CPU tensors -> is_cuda_graph_fully_compatible(gm) == True
```

### Earlier findings
- Must fix: the `get_handle` CPU node disabled CUDA graphs. **Resolved.** `test_hybridep_autograd_setup_keeps_cuda_graph_compatible` in graph_trainer's `test_passes.py` now guards it.
- Test placement: **resolved.** The test moved to `tests/unit_tests/cpu/distributed/test_expert_parallel.py`.
- Fold `capture` into the HybridEP helper: **resolved.**
- Duplicated handle-id cache in `deepep.py` and `hybridep.py`: **still open** (should consider). Both now point at remat#10, so the eventual removal is at least discoverable from either file.

### Must fix
1. PR description: "A CPU lookup op keeps autograd setup contexts traceable with FakeTensor/AOT" describes the op this revision deleted. Please replace it with the current mechanism: the backward ops take `handle_id`, and the cache is resolved inside the CUDA implementations.

### Should consider
- `tests/unit_tests/gpu/distributed/test_deepep_activation_checkpoint.py:264` -- the move into the shared harness dropped the explanatory DeepEP comments (see inline).

<details><summary>Details</summary>

- Lifetime: the cache entry stays alive while any of these references `handle_id`: `DispatchState`, the dispatch node's ctx, or the combine node's ctx. Without remat, `handle_id` is freed after backward frees the graph. Under `no_grad`, it is freed after combine. When remat replays the communication, the replayed dispatch creates its own id, and the replayed nodes' ctx keeps it. Because the region policy is `ep_communication`, dispatch and combine are always both saved or both replayed. A saved dispatch can never be paired with a replayed combine, so a missing `_handle_cache` key isn't reachable.
- No hidden sync: `.item()` reads a CPU tensor. Under CUDA-graph replay it runs only at capture time, the same as the previous opaque handle.
- The `ctx.handle_id` attribute doesn't create a reference cycle. `handle_id` is a non-differentiable int64 tensor with no `grad_fn`.
- Moving `test_passes.py` to `device="cuda"` under `FakeTensorMode` follows existing precedent in the same file (around line 3152).

</details>

Should consider: moving these tests into the shared harness also removed the comments explaining *why* DeepEP saves rather than replays. Atomics-ordered receive slots mean a replay can pair the wrong token gradients, and full remat is exact only because of the deterministic buffer. That reasoning is non-obvious and isn't written anywhere else in this file. Without it, `exact=bool(num_replays)` reads like an arbitrary choice. Please restore them. For example:

```suggestion
        # Backward would then pair each token's gradient with another token's
        # activations. These policies save dispatch and combine instead.
```

+# Choosing an expert-parallel backend
+
+TorchTitan supports two ways to execute routed experts: a token dispatcher
+followed by grouped expert computation, or Dist-MoE, which owns dispatch,
+expert computation, activation storage, and combine together. The router and
+checkpoint parameter names stay in TorchTitan.
+
+## Selection
+
+| Workload | Backend | Constraints |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| Correctness reference or a new accelerator | `AllToAllTokenDispatcher` | Uses PyTorch collectives. Variable token counts require a CPU sync; disable accelerator graphs. |
+| Quantized grouped GEMMs with the reference dispatcher | `TorchAOTokenDispatcher` | Adds per-expert padding to all-to-all. Also supports EP=1. |
+| NVIDIA training or inference with a separate grouped-GEMM implementation | `DeepEPTokenDispatcher` | Requires DeepEP v2. Training uses compact dispatch with a CPU sync; disable training accelerator graphs. Inference under `no_grad` can use `cuda_graph_compatible=True` for the static expand layout. |
+| NVIDIA training with graph-captured EP communication, including graph trainer | `HybridEPTokenDispatcher` | Requires the HybridEP branch and a supported NVLink/network topology. Set `non_blocking_capacity_factor` for CPU-free dispatch. |
+| Blackwell BF16 or MXFP8 training with integrated communication and compute | Dist-MoE | Requires SM100 or newer and `training.mixed_precision_param="bfloat16"`. Start with the [Dist-MoE recipes and runtime guide](../dist_moe/README.md). |
+
+Without expert parallelism, `LocalTokenDispatcher` only reorders local tokens.
+DeepEP and HybridEP require EP>1. TorchTitan does not expose a separate DeepEP
+v1 or direct NCCL EP dispatcher.
+
+HybridEP is developed by NVIDIA with CUDA graph support and has TorchTitan
+[graph-trainer](../../../experiments/graph_trainer/README.md) recipes and
+integration tests. DeepEP's graph-trainer compatibility has not been validated
+here; its current training adapter's CPU sync prevents CUDA graph capture.
+
+Both DeepEP v2 and HybridEP use NVIDIA-specific kernels and require a supported
+communication fabric. DeepEP v2 requires Hopper (SM90) or compatible newer GPUs;
+HybridEP uses TMA and targets Hopper/Blackwell systems. For other accelerators,
+start with the PyTorch all-to-all reference and check upstream hardware and
+fabric requirements before choosing an optimized backend.
+
+Choose by hardware, precision, graph requirements, and memory budget, then
+measure training step time and peak memory on the actual routing distribution.
+Dispatch/combine microbenchmarks alone do not measure overlap with expert GEMMs
+or the cost of activation rematerialization. Run at least 10 training steps so
+startup does not dominate the comparison.
+
+## Configure a dispatcher
+
+Use `TokenDispatcherTransform` to replace the dispatchers in an existing recipe:
+
+```python
+from torchtitan.config.transform import apply_transforms
+from torchtitan.config.transform.token_dispatcher import TokenDispatcherTransform
+from torchtitan.models.common.moe.token_dispatcher import HybridEPTokenDispatcher
+from torchtitan_recipes.models.deepseek_v3 import deepseek_v3_671b
+
+config = deepseek_v3_671b(seq_len=4096)
+config = apply_transforms(
+    config,
+    [
+        TokenDispatcherTransform(
+            dispatcher=HybridEPTokenDispatcher,
+            num_max_tokens_per_rank=(
+                config.training.num_tokens_per_microbatch_per_dp_rank
+                // (
+                    config.parallelism.context_parallel_degree
+                    * config.parallelism.tensor_parallel_degree
+                )
+            ),
+            kwargs={"non_blocking_capacity_factor": 1.0},
+        ),
+    ],
+)
+```
+
+`num_max_tokens_per_rank` bounds the input tokens one EP rank dispatches per
+forward for the lifetime of its communication buffer. It is not the number of
+tokens after top-k fan-out. Inference engines must use their own per-rank token
+budget. Dist-MoE uses `DistMoeTransform` and its runtime instead of this transform.
+
+For graph-captured training, also provide fixed-shape attention metadata and
+enable accelerator graphs as in the existing HybridEP recipes. A CPU-free
+dispatcher alone does not make the whole model capturable.
+
+### HybridEP capacity
+
+- `None`: blocking dispatch sizes the permuted output from actual token counts.
+- `1.0`: nonblocking dispatch reserves worst-case unpadded token fan-out, at a
+  higher memory cost.
+- Below `1.0`: a smaller permuted output can drop tokens on overflow. Load
+  balancing does not guarantee that arbitrary routing stays within capacity.
+
+The capacity factor sizes the permuted output, not the persistent communication
+buffer. Quantized experts also need the appropriate `pad_multiple`. Per-expert
+padding can overflow the allocation even at factor `1.0`. Check
+`check_hybridep_over_budget()` after the step for capacity below `1.0` or padded
+nonblocking dispatch, and reset the flag between measurements; it stays on the
+device until explicitly read.
+
+## Activation rematerialization
+
+The default remat policy saves dispatcher communication and recomputes the
+routed-expert `w13` projection. To retain communication under a custom policy:
+
+```python
+from torchtitan.distributed.activation_remat import ActivationRematConfig
+
+config.activation_remat = ActivationRematConfig(
+    save_regions=["*token_dispatcher.ep_communication"],
+)
+```
+
+DeepEP and HybridEP save or replay dispatch and combine together under
+`ep_communication`; selecting just its `.dispatch` or `.combine` suffix does
+not control the pair. Full remat replays both. DeepEP then enables deterministic
+receive ordering, adding a sort; HybridEP derives token positions from prefix
+scans. The all-to-all dispatcher instead has independent `dispatch` and
+`combine` regions that include local reordering and collectives.
+
+Dist-MoE always retains its outer region and owns its internal activation
+save/recompute decisions. See [REMAT.md](../../../distributed/REMAT.md) for
+policy details.
+
+## Dependencies
+
+DeepEP v2 and HybridEP currently live on incompatible branches of the same
+`deep_ep` package. Use separate environments when comparing them. Consult the
+upstream installation and fabric requirements:
+
+- [DeepEP v2](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/DeepEP)
+- [HybridEP](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/DeepEP/blob/hybrid-ep/docs/README_Hybrid-EP.md)
+- [Dist-MoE](../dist_moe/README.md)

**Verdict: Request changes** -- the new pure-CPU `hybridep.get_handle` op is traced into every HybridEP graph, and graph_trainer's all-or-nothing CUDA-graph gate rejects it. This would silently turn off CUDA graphs for the HybridEP graph-trainer recipe.

**What this PR does.** It wraps HybridEP dispatch and combine in `remat.region`s keyed by `ep_communication`, as DeepEP already does. Region outputs must be tensors, so the forward now returns a CPU `handle_id` instead of the opaque `DispatchHandle`; a module cache maps the id back to the handle. A new CPU custom op `hybridep.get_handle` resolves the id inside setup_context. The PR also adds an EP backend selection guide (`models/common/moe/README.md`), extends the DeepEP GPU remat test harness to HybridEP, and runs those tests in CI after the HybridEP installer.

**Example.** `graph_trainer_deepseek_v3_debugmodel_hybridep()` (`disable_accelerator_graphs = False`, nonblocking dispatch):
```
main:  dispatch -> getitem[3] (opaque handle) -> combine / combine_bwd
       every node CUDA-graph compatible -> cuda_graph_pass wraps the step
PR:    dispatch -> getitem[3] (CPU handle_id) -> hybridep.get_handle(handle_id)
       get_handle: only tensor is CPU -> is_cuda_graph_node_compatible == False
       -> "Skipping cuda_graph: graph is not compatible ..." (warning), eager step
```
In eager training with the default remat policy, the forward dispatch/combine pair is no longer replayed in backward (2+0 calls instead of 2+1), and the PR shows bitwise loss and grad_norm against main.

### Must fix
1. `torchtitan/distributed/deepep/hybridep.py:394` (and `:412`) -- `get_handle` in setup_context is a pure-CPU traced node, so graph_trainer skips CUDA graphs for HybridEP even without remat. CI won't catch it because both graph-trainer HybridEP integration tests disable accelerator graphs. Fix: delete `get_handle`, pass `handle_id` to `combine_bwd`/`dispatch_bwd`, save it with `save_for_backward`, and resolve the cache entry in the CUDA impls. This deletes the op and keeps FakeTensor tracing clean.

### Should consider
- `torchtitan/distributed/deepep/hybridep.py:217-221` -- duplicates DeepEP's handle-id cache scheme; share one helper so remat#10 removes it in one place.
- `tests/unit_tests/cpu/models/common/test_moe.py:165` -- tests `distributed/deepep/hybridep.py`; move it under `tests/unit_tests/cpu/distributed/`.
- `tests/unit_tests/gpu/distributed/test_deepep_activation_checkpoint.py:342` -- fold `capture` into `_check_hybridep_activation_checkpointing` instead of repeating the config.
- Scope: the backend selection guide is independent of the remat fix. Consider landing it separately so the remat fix can be reviewed on its own.

<details><summary>Details</summary>

- Gate: the problem is real on main. HybridEP's ops ran outside any region, so under `DefaultActivationRematConfig` they were recomputed (code outside regions is always recomputed), which contradicts the policy docstring. Fixing it in the dispatcher is the right layer, and the opaque-output workaround has a TODO pointing at meta-pytorch/remat#10.
- Why the gate fires: `_iter_tensors` returns `[]` for the opaque `DispatchHandle` output, and the input `handle_id` FakeTensor is on CPU, so `all(t.device.type == "cpu")` holds. `dispatch` and `combine` themselves stay compatible because they mix CUDA and CPU tensors. `cuda_graph_pass` calls `is_cuda_graph_compatible(gm)` and returns `gm` unwrapped on any incompatible node.
- With the proposed fix, `combine_bwd`/`dispatch_bwd` each take a CUDA grad plus the CPU id and stay compatible. Their arg positions are unchanged for `paged_stash_memory_policy.py`, which matches on `combine_bwd` by `seq_nr`. Under CUDA graph replay the impls' `.item()` runs only at capture time, which matches today's opaque-handle behaviour.
- README claims spot-checked against code: dispatcher class names, `TokenDispatcherTransform` path, `deepseek_v3_671b(seq_len=...)`, `check_hybridep_over_budget`, Dist-MoE SM100/bf16 requirement, and default save/recompute regions all exist as described.

</details>

**Verdict: Approve -- please address the items below before merging.** The CUDA-graph regression from the last review is fixed: `hybridep.get_handle` is gone, and a new graph_trainer test guards against it coming back.

**What changed since the last review.** The backward ops (`combine_bwd`, `dispatch_bwd`) now take `handle_id: Tensor`, the same way `combine` does. They resolve `_handle_cache[handle_id.item()]` only inside the real CUDA implementations, so setup_context no longer traces a CPU-only op. setup_context keeps `handle_id` as a ctx attribute rather than calling `save_for_backward`. The reason is that saved-tensor hooks could copy the tensor and let the original, which owns the cache entry, be collected. The GPU test exercises this with a cloning `saved_tensors_hooks`.

**Example.** `graph_trainer_deepseek_v3_debugmodel_hybridep()` traced graph:
```
previous rev: dispatch -> handle_id -> hybridep.get_handle(handle_id)   # pure-CPU node -> cuda_graph skipped
HEAD:         dispatch -> handle_id -> combine(x, handle_id) / combine_bwd(g, s, handle_id)
              every node mixes CUDA and CPU tensors -> is_cuda_graph_fully_compatible(gm) == True
```

### Earlier findings
- Must fix: the `get_handle` CPU node disabled CUDA graphs. **Resolved.** `test_hybridep_autograd_setup_keeps_cuda_graph_compatible` in graph_trainer's `test_passes.py` now guards it.
- Test placement: **resolved.** The test moved to `tests/unit_tests/cpu/distributed/test_expert_parallel.py`.
- Fold `capture` into the HybridEP helper: **resolved.**
- Duplicated handle-id cache in `deepep.py` and `hybridep.py`: **still open** (should consider). Both now point at remat#10, so the eventual removal is at least discoverable from either file.

### Must fix
1. PR description: "A CPU lookup op keeps autograd setup contexts traceable with FakeTensor/AOT" describes the op this revision deleted. Please replace it with the current mechanism: the backward ops take `handle_id`, and the cache is resolved inside the CUDA implementations.

### Should consider
- `tests/unit_tests/gpu/distributed/test_deepep_activation_checkpoint.py:264` -- the move into the shared harness dropped the explanatory DeepEP comments (see inline).

<details><summary>Details</summary>

- Lifetime: the cache entry stays alive while any of these references `handle_id`: `DispatchState`, the dispatch node's ctx, or the combine node's ctx. Without remat, `handle_id` is freed after backward frees the graph. Under `no_grad`, it is freed after combine. When remat replays the communication, the replayed dispatch creates its own id, and the replayed nodes' ctx keeps it. Because the region policy is `ep_communication`, dispatch and combine are always both saved or both replayed. A saved dispatch can never be paired with a replayed combine, so a missing `_handle_cache` key isn't reachable.
- No hidden sync: `.item()` reads a CPU tensor. Under CUDA-graph replay it runs only at capture time, the same as the previous opaque handle.
- The `ctx.handle_id` attribute doesn't create a reference cycle. `handle_id` is a non-differentiable int64 tensor with no `grad_fn`.
- Moving `test_passes.py` to `device="cuda"` under `FakeTensorMode` follows existing precedent in the same file (around line 3152).

</details>
